long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Jizzakh, Uzbekistan, Chodiev studied international law and Japanese at MGIMO before working on Soviet-Japanese commercial relations. He later joined Alexander Machkevich and Alijan Ibragimov in assembling metals, mining, energy and logistics businesses across Kazakhstan. Their enterprise developed into ENRC, whose flotation in London established an international public-market profile before the founders and Kazakhstan's government took it private. ERG succeeded that platform as an integrated resources group with assets spanning extraction, processing, power and transport.

Chodiev's relationship with ERG later shifted from founder-director to former shareholder. He was replaced on the board in 2024 and disposed of his 18.6% holding in 2026. Separately, he established the International Chodiev Foundation to support education, social assistance, arts and cultural exchange. Its programs include MGIMO scholarships, social-support projects in Central Asia and preservation of Japan's Itchiku Kubota kimono collection.

uncertainties: Patokh Chodiev is the established English form used by Forbes, ERG and his foundation. Patokh Shodiev and Fattokh Kayumovich Shodiev are transliteration variants tied to the same birth details and career, not separate identities.

Kayumovich is not proposed as a live middle-name update because authoritative English-language sources omit the patronymic and transliteration conventions vary. It remains a review candidate below the acceptance threshold.

ERG's July 2024 announcement describes Sabir Chodiev replacing Patokh Chodiev on the board, while its 2023 sustainability report gives April 2024 for that change. The dossier uses the more specific April date only in supporting analysis and states the year in the biographies.

ERG announced in May 2026 that Chodiev sold his entire remaining 18.6% shareholding. Older Forbes and foundation pages that call him a current part owner or co-owner are therefore superseded on present ownership.

Primary industry is Unknown because the final ERG divestment removed the only well-documented dominant commercial holding and no reliable source identifies the principal deployment of the sale proceeds. Finance and Investments remains a plausible but unverified candidate.
Metals and Mining remains the wealth-creation industry because ENRC and ERG created the fortune; the later sale does not change its origin sector.

Founder remains the wealth relationship because Chodiev created the core enterprise. His completed governance and ownership exits are stated explicitly to avoid implying a current operating or shareholder role.

Self-made is used at the broad level because Forbes explicitly applies that classification and the founder-built mechanism is clear, while the evidence does not adequately establish whether his start was independent or materially advantaged.

The International Chodiev Foundation is accepted as a personal website because it is eponymous, identifies Chodiev as founder and documents his ongoing public program interests. It is not treated as a current wealth-producing industry.

The input's Russian nationality and United Kingdom residence are not corrected because citizenship and residence claims vary over time and those fields fall outside the accepted evidence set for this scope.
The existing Wikipedia profile is exact and retained. No exact personal LinkedIn or Instagram account met the verification threshold.
